problem: No public dataset combines multiple indoor scene types, continuous differential-drive expert actions, language instructions, and multi-modal per-step observations (RGB, depth, segmentation). Existing VLN-CE, ObjectNav and ALFRED data are single-scene, use discrete actions, lack language, or target manipulation.
motivation: VLA models need large demonstration sets, but real-robot demonstrations are expensive. Simulation gives cheap, perfectly annotated demonstrations for wheeled language-conditioned navigation, and structured OOD splits enable systematic generalization study.
key_idea: Release a 1,174-episode Isaac Sim dataset for Language-Conditioned Object Approach with a Nova Carter robot, using a proportional expert, tiered spawn distances, and five splits covering paraphrase and held-out-object OOD.
insight: This is a dataset paper with no learned baselines, so the only evidence is descriptive statistics. Spawn distance correlates with trajectory length (Pearson r=0.94, slope ~1.00), and far-tier episodes are 2.9x longer than near-tier. The authors themselves note this reflects a near-straight expert path rather than difficulty diversity. Heavy imbalance (monitor, rack, crate = 62.1% of episodes), 14 far-tier episodes, and selection bias toward unobstructed paths limit how much the dataset can test language grounding.
method: Simulation and robot: NVIDIA Isaac Sim 5.1 with a Nova Carter differential-drive robot, front stereo camera at 640x640, 60 Hz; 4 scenes (Office, Hospital, Full Warehouse, Warehouse Multi-Shelf).
Target discovery: traverse the USD stage and match prim names against 12 category rules; cache 3-D bounding-box centroids per scene.
Tiered spawn sampling: near 1.5-3.5 m (30%), mid 3.5-7 m (40%), far from global curated points (30%); spawn validated by a displacement check after physics warmup.
Language templates: 18 train and 12 paraphrase-OOD slot templates. Color-slot templates are suppressed because all targets have color=unknown, leaving 13 train and 10 OOD active.

Expert controller: proportional control from the segmentation-mask centroid and median depth (k_omega=1.4, k_v=0.7). Falls back to a bearing-only law from the known goal when the target is not visible, plus a depth-based obstacle clamp.
Episode archiving: only successful episodes (within 1 m, stopped for 5 steps) are kept, with RGB, depth, segmentation, continuous and 7x7-tokenized actions, poses, and meta.json.
Splits: five splits (train_id 716, val_id 114, test_id 121, test_paraphrase_ood 122, test_ood_obj 101) stratified per scene.

setting.backbone: none (dataset paper; expert is a hand-designed proportional controller, no trained baselines)
setting.training_data: none; the paper releases a dataset of 1,174 expert episodes and reports no model training
setting.observation: front RGB 640x640 + metric depth + instance segmentation (RGB-D used as policy input)
setting.action_space: continuous (v in [0,1] m/s, omega in [-1.5,1.5] rad/s), tokenized to 7x7=49 bins
setting.privileged: expert uses GT segmentation masks and known goal position for data generation; success is judged against the GT 3-D goal centroid

numbers_note: No model results. Only dataset statistics are reported (e.g., mean NE 0.967 m of the expert's successful episodes), and baselines are deferred to a companion paper.
results: The dataset has 1,174 validated episodes (Office 700, Hospital 52, Full Warehouse 354, Multi-Shelf 68), mean trajectory length 2.74 m, and mean 200.9 steps. Spawn distance vs trajectory length gives r=0.94. Tier counts are 640 near, 520 mid, and 14 far. No agent baselines are evaluated.
limitations: Far-tier is only 1.2% of episodes; category imbalance (three categories = 62.1%); all color templates unusable (color=unknown).
Proportional expert has only 40-60% attempt success in Hospital/Warehouse, causing selection bias toward unobstructed paths.
Static scenes, single camera, sim-to-real gap, and no trained baselines reported.
